```{r}
# Load libraries

# Package versions are recorded in renv.lock. After cloning the repository, run renv::restore() once to install exactly those versions; the library() calls below then load them. (pacman::p_load() is no longer used, because it silently installs the newest version of any missing package and so bypasses renv.)

# DATA HANDLING#
library(here)        # for building file paths from the project root (the folder holding the .Rproj file)
library(tidyverse)   # for data manipulation, cleaning, and visualisation in a cohesive framework (dplyr, tidyr, purrr, ggplot2, forcats)
library(zoo)         # for working with ordered observations = 5-year rolling means

# SPATIAL DATA & MAPPING#
library(sf)          # for handling vector spatial data (points, lines, polygons)
library(terra)       # for handling and processing raster data
library(tidyterra)   # for using tidyverse tools on terra objects (geom_spatraster)
library(tmap)        # for creating thematic maps
library(ggspatial)   # for adding scale bars and north arrows to maps built with ggplot2

# VISUALISATION#
library(viridis)     # for perceptually uniform, colour-blind-friendly colour palettes
library(scales)      # for controlling plot scale formatting (e.g., number labels)
library(hexbin)      # for visualising point density with hexagonal bins (needed by geom_hex)
library(scico)       # for scientific colour maps
library(patchwork)   # for combining multiple plots into one figure
library(ggridges)    # for creating ridgeline plots
library(grid)        # for units and image panels inside figures
library(flextable)   # for creating publication-quality tables saved as Word documents

# STATISTICAL ANALYSIS#
library(trend)       # for analysing trends in time-series data = Theil-Sen slope
```

```{r}
# Interactive (leaflet) maps are useful when running chunks one at a time in RStudio, but they make the knitted document very large and slow. Maps are therefore interactive in an interactive session and static when the document is knitted.

Map.Mode <- if (interactive()) "view" else "plot"
```

```{r}
# Project paths 
# All inputs are read relative to the project root, which "here" resolves from the .Rproj file. No absolute paths are used, so the analysis runs unchanged on any machine once data/ is populated as described in the README.

dir_data    <- here::here("data")
dir_rpi <- file.path(dir_data, "RPI Datasets (GuyLomax)")
dir_borders <- file.path(dir_data, "Country_Borders")
dir_wdpa    <- file.path(dir_data, "WDPA_Amboseli_Tsavo", "National Parks&Reserves")
dir_amb     <- file.path(dir_data, "Amboseli_Conservation_Areas")
dir_tsv     <- file.path(dir_data, "Tsavo_Conservation_Areas")

# Figures and tables are written to plots/ (created here if it does not exist yet)
dir.create(here::here("plots"), showWarnings = FALSE)

# Helper for WDPA downloads, which keep their original nested folder structure.
# The numeric argument is the WDPA site ID (April 2025 release).
wdpa_path <- function(name, id) {
  file.path(dir_wdpa,
            paste0(name, "-WDPA_WDOECM_Apr2025_Public_", id, "_shp"),
            paste0("WDPA_WDOECM_Apr2025_Public_", id, "_shp_0"),
            paste0("WDPA_WDOECM_Apr2025_Public_", id, "_shp-polygons.shp"))
}

required_dirs <- c(dir_rpi, dir_borders, dir_wdpa, dir_amb, dir_tsv)
missing_dirs  <- required_dirs[!dir.exists(required_dirs)]
if (length(missing_dirs) > 0) {
  stop("Input data not found. Missing directories:\n  ",
       paste(missing_dirs, collapse = "\n  "),
       "\n\nSee the 'Obtaining the data' section of README.md for sources.",
       call. = FALSE)
}
```

```{r}
# Set theme for plots

theme_beautiful <- function() {
  theme_bw() +
    theme(
      text = element_text(family = "Helvetica"),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 8, color = "black"),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 8, color = "black"),
      axis.line.x = element_line(linewidth = 0.3, color = "black"), # Use linewidth
      axis.line.y = element_line(linewidth = 0.3, color = "black"), # Use linewidth
      axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = 0.3, color = "black"), # Use linewidth
      panel.border = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      plot.margin = unit(c(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5), "cm"),
      plot.title = element_text(
        size = 8,
        vjust = 1,
        hjust = 0.5,
        color = "black"
      ),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 8, color = "black"),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 8, color = "black"),
      legend.position = "right", # Move legend to the right
      legend.key.size = unit(0.9, "line"),
      legend.background = element_rect(
        color = "black",
        fill = "transparent",
        linewidth = 0.3, # Use linewidth
        linetype = "blank"
      )
    )
}

# Attempt to set the Helvetica font (may not work on all systems)
if (Sys.info()[["sysname"]] == "Windows") {
  windowsFonts("Helvetica" = windowsFont("Helvetica"))
}
```

```{r}
# Importing RPI Datasets - Rasters (TIFs)

Actual.GPP <- rast(file.path(dir_rpi, "actual_gpp_ea_v2.tif"))

Potential.GPP <- rast(file.path(dir_rpi, "potential_gpp_ea_v2.tif"))

RPI <- rast(file.path(dir_rpi, "rpi_ea_v2.tif"))

# The RPI v2 series covers 23 hydrological years (September 2000 to August 2023). Layers are named by the start year of each hydrological year (rpi.2000 to rpi.2022).
stopifnot(nlyr(RPI) == 23)
```

```{r}
# Importing the temporal performance layers (MAE, RMSE, R²) supplied with the RPI v2 product

# These are imported here, before any zone is processed, so that the R² quality-control filter can be applied once, straight after each zone is cropped. Every later step (yearly zone means, Theil-Sen slopes, figures and tables) then uses the same retained pixels.

Temporal.Performance <- rast(file.path(dir_rpi, "rpi_ea_temporal_performance.tif"))

## Extract R² layer
RSQ.Layer <- Temporal.Performance[["rsq"]]

# The R² and RPI layers are on the same grid (same extent, resolution, origin and CRS), so the R² layer can simply be cropped to each zone; no resampling is needed
stopifnot(compareGeom(RSQ.Layer, RPI))

# Published quality-control threshold: pixels with R² < 0.1 are excluded from the analysis. Any positive R² represents an improvement over using raw GPP or NDVI; 0.1 excludes pixels where the quantile regression forest explains little or none of the year-to-year variation in GPP. The share of pixels retained in each zone is calculated in "Pixel.Retention.Table".
RSQ.Threshold.1 <- 0.1
```

```{r}
# MAPS SOURCED FROM WDPA
```


```{r}
# Importing Community Conservancies & Group Ranches surrounding Amboseli

AET.Conservancies <- st_read(file.path(dir_amb, "AET_Conservancies.shp"))

AET.Buffers <- st_read(file.path(dir_amb, "AET_Other_Conserved_Areas.shp"))
```

```{r}
# Importing Community Conservancies & Group Ranches surrounding Tsavos

Tsavo.Ranches <- st_read(file.path(dir_tsv, "RanchesTTWCA.shp"))

Tsavo.SettledAreas <- st_read(file.path(dir_tsv, "SettledAreas.shp"))
```

```{r}
# One rule for which pixels belong to each governance zone

# The zone polygons come from three different sources and overlap in places (the overlaps are listed in "Zone.Overlaps.Before" below). Left as supplied, a pixel inside an overlap would be analysed in two zones. The steps below make sure every pixel is assigned to exactly one zone:
#   1. All zone polygons are put in one projected CRS and their geometries are repaired.
#   2. Overlaps between polygons of the same zone are removed, so no pixel is counted twice within a zone.
#   3. Overlaps between zones are given to one zone only, in this order of precedence:
#        Amboseli: National Park > Conservancies > Community/Group Ranches
#        Tsavo:    National Parks > Conservancies/Ranches > Settled Areas
#   4. The cleaned polygons are returned in the CRS of the RPI grid.
# Later on, mask(..., touches = FALSE) and extract() both keep a pixel only when its centre lies inside a polygon, so the maps, the tables and the trend analysis all use the same pixels.

# Polygon overlaps and areas are worked out in a projected CRS (UTM zone 37S, in metres), where planar geometry is appropriate
Zone.Projected.CRS <- 32737

# Step 1: Common projected CRS and valid geometries
clean_zone <- function(x) {
  x %>%
    st_transform(Zone.Projected.CRS) %>%
    st_make_valid()
}

Amboseli           <- clean_zone(Amboseli)
TsavoEast          <- clean_zone(TsavoEast)
TsavoWest          <- clean_zone(TsavoWest)
AET.Conservancies  <- clean_zone(AET.Conservancies)
AET.Buffers        <- clean_zone(AET.Buffers)
Tsavo.Ranches      <- clean_zone(Tsavo.Ranches)
Tsavo.SettledAreas <- clean_zone(Tsavo.SettledAreas)

# Area of a zone in km² (its polygons are merged first, so nothing is counted twice)
area_km2 <- function(x) {
  x <- st_union(st_transform(st_geometry(x), Zone.Projected.CRS))
  sum(as.numeric(st_area(x))) / 1e6
}

# Area shared by two zones in km²
overlap_km2 <- function(a, b) {
  a <- st_union(st_transform(st_geometry(a), Zone.Projected.CRS))
  b <- st_union(st_transform(st_geometry(b), Zone.Projected.CRS))
  shared <- st_intersection(a, b)
  if (length(shared) == 0) 0 else sum(as.numeric(st_area(shared))) / 1e6
}

# Table of the overlap between every pair of zones
zone_overlaps <- function(zones) {
  combn(names(zones), 2, simplify = FALSE) %>%
    map_dfr(function(pair) {
      tibble(
        ZoneA = pair[1],
        ZoneB = pair[2],
        Overlap_km2 = round(overlap_km2(zones[[pair[1]]], zones[[pair[2]]]), 2)
      )
    }) %>%
    filter(Overlap_km2 >= 0.01) %>%
    arrange(desc(Overlap_km2))
}

# Recording the overlaps in the polygons as supplied, before they are removed
Zone.Overlaps.Before <- zone_overlaps(list(
  "Amboseli NP" = Amboseli,
  "Amboseli Conservancies" = AET.Conservancies,
  "Amboseli Community/Group Ranches" = AET.Buffers,
  "Tsavo East NP" = TsavoEast,
  "Tsavo West NP" = TsavoWest,
  "Tsavo Conservancies/Ranches" = Tsavo.Ranches,
  "Tsavo Settled Areas" = Tsavo.SettledAreas
))

Zone.Overlaps.Before

# Steps 2 and 3: Remove overlaps within a zone, then overlaps with the zones that take precedence
make_exclusive <- function(x, ...) {

  # Within the zone: each polygon loses any part already covered by an earlier polygon of the same zone
  x <- st_difference(x)

  # Between zones: remove the parts covered by the zones that take precedence
  higher <- list(...)
  if (length(higher) > 0) {
    higher <- st_union(do.call(c, lapply(higher, st_geometry)))
    x <- suppressWarnings(st_difference(x, higher))
  }

  # Keep polygons only and drop anything left empty
  x <- suppressWarnings(st_collection_extract(st_make_valid(x), "POLYGON"))
  x[!st_is_empty(x), ]
}

AET.Conservancies  <- make_exclusive(AET.Conservancies, Amboseli, TsavoWest)
AET.Buffers        <- make_exclusive(AET.Buffers, Amboseli, AET.Conservancies)
Tsavo.Ranches      <- make_exclusive(Tsavo.Ranches, TsavoEast, TsavoWest)
Tsavo.SettledAreas <- make_exclusive(Tsavo.SettledAreas, TsavoEast, TsavoWest, Tsavo.Ranches)

# Check: no overlap should remain between any two zones
Zone.Overlaps.After <- zone_overlaps(list(
  "Amboseli NP" = Amboseli,
  "Amboseli Conservancies" = AET.Conservancies,
  "Amboseli Community/Group Ranches" = AET.Buffers,
  "Tsavo East NP" = TsavoEast,
  "Tsavo West NP" = TsavoWest,
  "Tsavo Conservancies/Ranches" = Tsavo.Ranches,
  "Tsavo Settled Areas" = Tsavo.SettledAreas
))

stopifnot(nrow(Zone.Overlaps.After) == 0)

# Step 4: Back to the CRS of the RPI grid
Amboseli           <- st_transform(Amboseli, crs(RPI))
TsavoEast          <- st_transform(TsavoEast, crs(RPI))
TsavoWest          <- st_transform(TsavoWest, crs(RPI))
AET.Conservancies  <- st_transform(AET.Conservancies, crs(RPI))
AET.Buffers        <- st_transform(AET.Buffers, crs(RPI))
Tsavo.Ranches      <- st_transform(Tsavo.Ranches, crs(RPI))
Tsavo.SettledAreas <- st_transform(Tsavo.SettledAreas, crs(RPI))

# Check: every polygon is valid for terra, which does the masking and extraction
stopifnot(
  all(is.valid(vect(Amboseli))), all(is.valid(vect(TsavoEast))), all(is.valid(vect(TsavoWest))),
  all(is.valid(vect(AET.Conservancies))), all(is.valid(vect(AET.Buffers))),
  all(is.valid(vect(Tsavo.Ranches))), all(is.valid(vect(Tsavo.SettledAreas)))
)
```

```{r}
# Visualising the Conservancies & Community Lands within AET

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = Kenya.Admin.Boundary, fill = "grey95", color = "black") +
  geom_sf(data = AET.Buffers, aes(fill = "Amboseli Community Lands"), alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_sf(data = AET.Conservancies, aes(fill = "Amboseli Conservancies"), alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_sf(data = Amboseli, aes(fill = "Amboseli NP"), alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = "Land Use Types",
    values = c(
      "Amboseli Community Lands" = "orange",
      "Amboseli Conservancies" = "maroon",
      "Amboseli NP" = "darkgreen"
    )
  ) +
  annotation_scale(location = "bl") +
  annotation_north_arrow(location = "tl") +
  theme_beautiful() +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
```

```{r}
## Visualising Amboseli NP

# Crop to the zone, then keep only the pixels whose centre lies inside the boundary (touches = FALSE), the same rule that extract() applies later
Amboseli.RPI.Crop.Unfiltered <- mask(crop(RPI, Amboseli, snap = "out"), Amboseli, touches = FALSE)

# Averaging across years for visualization (all pixels in the zone, before quality control)
Amboseli.RPI.Mean <- mean(Amboseli.RPI.Crop.Unfiltered, na.rm = TRUE)

# Quality control: crop the R² layer to the same cells (same grid, so no resampling) and drop pixels with R² < 0.1
RSQ.Amboseli <- crop(RSQ.Layer, Amboseli.RPI.Crop.Unfiltered)
stopifnot(compareGeom(RSQ.Amboseli, Amboseli.RPI.Crop.Unfiltered))
Amboseli.RPI.Crop <- mask(Amboseli.RPI.Crop.Unfiltered, RSQ.Amboseli >= RSQ.Threshold.1, maskvalues = FALSE)

# Mean RPI of the retained pixels (R² ≥ 0.1), used for all results reported in the manuscript
Amboseli.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1 <- mean(Amboseli.RPI.Crop, na.rm = TRUE)

# Visualise
tmap_mode(Map.Mode)
tm_shape(Amboseli.RPI.Mean) +
  tm_raster(col.scale = tm_scale_continuous(values = "viridis"), 
            col.legend = tm_legend(title = "Mean RPI", reverse = TRUE)) +
  tm_shape(Amboseli) +
  tm_borders(col = "white", lwd = 2) +
  tm_title("Spatial Distribution of Mean RPI in Amboseli NP") +
  tm_layout(legend.outside = TRUE)
```

```{r}
## Extracting RPI for Amboseli NP

Amboseli.RPI.Values.Full <- terra::extract(Amboseli.RPI.Crop, Amboseli, cells = TRUE)

### Remove ID column (first column added by extract)
Amboseli.RPI.Values <- Amboseli.RPI.Values.Full[, names(Amboseli.RPI.Crop)]

Amboseli.Summary <- data.frame(
  Layer = names(Amboseli.RPI.Crop),
  Mean = apply(Amboseli.RPI.Values, 2, mean, na.rm = TRUE),
  SD = apply(Amboseli.RPI.Values, 2, sd, na.rm = TRUE),
  Q25 = apply(Amboseli.RPI.Values, 2, quantile, probs = 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
  Median = apply(Amboseli.RPI.Values, 2, median, na.rm = TRUE),
  Q75 = apply(Amboseli.RPI.Values, 2, quantile, probs = 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
)

print(Amboseli.Summary)
```

```{r}
Tsavo.AllZones.RPI.Values.Full <- terra::extract(Tsavo.AllZones.RPI.Crop, Tsavo.AllZones, cells= TRUE)

Tsavo.AllZones.RPI.Values <- Tsavo.AllZones.RPI.Values.Full[, names(Tsavo.AllZones.RPI.Crop)]

Tsavo.AllZones.Summary <- data.frame(
  Layer = names(Tsavo.AllZones.RPI.Crop),
  Mean = apply(Tsavo.AllZones.RPI.Values, 2, mean, na.rm = TRUE),
  SD = apply(Tsavo.AllZones.RPI.Values, 2, sd, na.rm = TRUE),
  Q25 = apply(Tsavo.AllZones.RPI.Values, 2, quantile, probs = 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
  Median = apply(Tsavo.AllZones.RPI.Values, 2, median, na.rm = TRUE),
  Q75 = apply(Tsavo.AllZones.RPI.Values, 2, quantile, probs = 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
)

print(Tsavo.AllZones.Summary)
```

```{r}
# Visualising Extracted RPI Values
```

```{r}
## Visualising Amboseli NP

Amboseli.RPI.Visual <- Amboseli.RPI.Values %>%
  mutate(ID = row_number()) %>%  # optional, to keep track of pixels
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -ID,                 # exclude ID column from pivoting
    names_to = "Layer",
    values_to = "RPI_value"
  ) %>%
  # Keep only layers starting with "rpi."
  filter(grepl("^rpi\\.", Layer)) %>%
  mutate(
    Year = as.integer(sub("rpi\\.", "", Layer)),
    Area = "Amboseli"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Year) & !is.na(RPI_value)) %>%  # remove NA years or RPI values
  select(ID, Area, Year, RPI_value) ## I will need "ID" for Trend Analysis (Theil-Sen)

# Now plot
ggplot(Amboseli.RPI.Visual, aes(x = factor(Year), y = RPI_value)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightblue", outlier.color = "red") +
  labs(
    title = "RPI Distribution Over Years in Amboseli NP",
    x = "Year",
    y = "RPI Value"
  ) +
  theme_beautiful()
```

```{r}
## Visualising Amboseli NP (using a Violin Plot)

ggplot(Amboseli.RPI.Visual, aes(x = factor(Year), y = RPI_value)) +
  geom_violin(fill = "lightblue", color = "black", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, outlier.color = "red", alpha = 0.5) +  # optional: overlay boxplot for summary stats
  labs(
    title = "RPI Distribution Over Years in Amboseli NP (Violin Plot)",
    x = "Year",
    y = "RPI Value"
  ) +
  theme_beautiful()
```

```{r}
## Conversation on refining the Violin plots:

# 1.Skepticism about RPI Fluctuations:
# Do not fully trust year-to-year fluctuations in the (RPI).

#2.Focus on Comparisons:
# Emphasise comparisons in:
# (i) Average performance
# (ii) Trends over time
# Analyse these comparisons across different spatial units and/or management periods.

# 3. Signal vs. Noise:
# Aim to focus on the real signal rather than the noise in the data.

# 4. Outlier Classification:
# Recommend including arguments against disabling "outlier" classification.
# Suggest that there are insufficient grounds to treat the red dots differently.
```

```{r}
## Visualising Amboseli NP

ggplot(Amboseli.RPI.Visual, aes(x = factor(Year), y = RPI_value)) +
  geom_violin(fill = "lightblue", color = "black", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.4) +  # removes red outlier dots
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "line", aes(group = 1), color = "darkblue", linewidth = 0.6) + #Added mean line to get the general pattern
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", shape = 21, fill = "purple", size = 2) + # Combined the mean line with points to make it easier to visualise
  labs(
    title = "RPI Distribution Over Years in Amboseli NP (Violin Plot)",
    x = "Year",
    y = "RPI Value"
  ) +
  theme_beautiful()
```

```{r}
## Visualising Mean RPI over Amboseli NP as a line 

Amboseli.Mean <- Amboseli.RPI.Visual %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  summarise(Mean_RPI = mean(RPI_value, na.rm = TRUE))

ggplot(Amboseli.Mean, aes(x = Year, y = Mean_RPI)) +
  geom_line(color = "darkgreen", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(color = "black", fill = "purple", shape = 21, size = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean RPI Over Time in Amboseli NP",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Mean RPI"
  ) +
  theme_beautiful()
```

```{r}
# Creating each of the 9 individual plots and storing them in a variable

Amboseli.Violin.Plot <- ggplot(Amboseli.RPI.Visual, aes(x = factor(Year), y = RPI_value)) +
  geom_violin(fill = "lightblue", color = "black", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.4) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "line", aes(group = 1), color = "darkblue", linewidth = 0.6) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", shape = 21, fill = "purple", size = 2) +

  ggtitle("Amboseli NP") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

AET.Buffers.Violin.Plot <- ggplot(AET.Buffers.RPI.Visual, aes(x = factor(Year), y = RPI_value)) +
  geom_violin(fill = "lightblue", color = "black", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.4) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "line", aes(group = 1), color = "darkblue", linewidth = 0.6) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", shape = 21, fill = "purple", size = 2) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "RPI Value") +
  ggtitle("AET Buffers") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

AET.AllZones.Violin.Plot <- ggplot(AET.AllZones.RPI.Visual, aes(x = factor(Year), y = RPI_value)) +
  geom_violin(fill = "lightblue", color = "black", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.4) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "line", aes(group = 1), color = "darkblue", linewidth = 0.6) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", shape = 21, fill = "purple", size = 2) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "RPI Value") +
  ggtitle("AET All Zones") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# Arrange plots in a 3x3 grid
Combined.RPI.Violin.Plots <- (
  Amboseli.Violin.Plot + TsavoEast.Violin.Plot + TsavoWest.Violin.Plot
) / (
  Tsavo.Ranches.Violin.Plot + Tsavo.SettledAreas.Violin.Plot + Tsavo.AllZones.Violin.Plot
) / (
  AET.Conservancies.Violin.Plot + AET.Buffers.Violin.Plot + AET.AllZones.Violin.Plot
)

# Rotate x-axis labels & control subplot theme
Combined.RPI.Violin.Plots <- Combined.RPI.Violin.Plots &
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 9),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 11),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 11)
  )

# Add title/subtitle/caption with smaller sizes
Combined.RPI.Violin.Plots <- Combined.RPI.Violin.Plots +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "RPI Distribution Over Years by Zone (Violin Plots)",
    subtitle = "Showing median, interquartile range, and mean trend line",
    caption = "Each panel shows RPI values by year. Violin width represents distribution density.\nBoxplot overlay shows IQR, whiskers, and median; purple dots and lines show means.",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 16, hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5),
      plot.caption = element_text(size = 9, hjust = 0.5)
    )
  )

# Adjust geoms globally (example if you use consistent geoms across plots)
scale_geom_defaults <- function() {
  update_geom_defaults("violin", list(size = 0.4))
  update_geom_defaults("boxplot", list(size = 0.3))
  update_geom_defaults("point", list(size = 1.5, colour = "purple"))
  update_geom_defaults("line", list(size = 0.4, colour = "purple"))
}
scale_geom_defaults()

# Print
Combined.RPI.Violin.Plots
```

```{r}
# 5 year rolling mean Amboseli
Amboseli.Mean <- Amboseli.RPI.Visual %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  summarise(Mean_RPI = mean(RPI_value, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(Year) %>%
  mutate(RollingMean5 = zoo::rollmean(Mean_RPI, k = 5, fill = NA, align = "center"))

ggplot(Amboseli.Mean, aes(x = Year)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Mean_RPI), color = "grey60", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_line(aes(y = RollingMean5), color = "red", linewidth = 1.2) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean RPI with 5-Year Rolling Mean (Amboseli)",
    x = "Year", y = "Mean RPI"
  ) + theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

```

```{r}
ggplot() +
  geom_violin(data = Amboseli.RPI.Visual,
              aes(x = Year, y = RPI_value, group = Year, fill = "Distribution"),
              color = "black", alpha = 0.5, width = 0.8) +
  geom_line(data = Amboseli.Mean,
            aes(x = Year, y = RollingMean5, color = "5-Year Rolling Mean"),
            linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(data = Amboseli.Mean,
             aes(x = Year, y = RollingMean5, color = "5-Year Rolling Mean"),
             size = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Amboseli RPI Distribution with 5-Year Rolling Mean",
    x = "Year",
    y = "RPI Value",
    fill = "Legend",
    color = "Legend"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Distribution" = "lightblue")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("5-Year Rolling Mean" = "darkblue")) +
  theme_beautiful()
```

```{r}
# Binding all the above & Removing "All Zones" at source
All.RPI.Visual.Areas <- bind_rows(
  Amboseli.RPI.Visual %>% mutate(Area = "Amboseli Park"),
  TsavoEast.RPI.Visual %>% mutate(Area = "Tsavo East"),
  TsavoWest.RPI.Visual %>% mutate(Area = "Tsavo West"),
  Tsavo.Ranches.RPI.Visual %>% mutate(Area = "Tsavo Ranches"),
  Tsavo.SettledAreas.RPI.Visual %>% mutate(Area = "Tsavo Settled Areas"),
  AET.Conservancies.RPI.Visual %>% mutate(Area = "AET Conservancies"),
  AET.Buffers.RPI.Visual %>% mutate(Area = "AET Buffers")
)

All.Means <- bind_rows(
  Amboseli.Mean %>% mutate(Area = "Amboseli Park"),
  TsavoEast.Mean %>% mutate(Area = "Tsavo East"),
  TsavoWest.Mean %>% mutate(Area = "Tsavo West"),
  Tsavo.Ranches.Mean %>% mutate(Area = "Tsavo Ranches"),
  Tsavo.SettledAreas.Mean %>% mutate(Area = "Tsavo Settled Areas"),
  AET.Conservancies.Mean %>% mutate(Area = "AET Conservancies"),
  AET.Buffers.Mean %>% mutate(Area = "AET Buffers")
)

# Apply new labels and similar colours
area_labels.noAllZones <- c(
  "Amboseli Park" = "Amboseli NP",
  "AET Buffers" = "Amboseli Community/Group Ranches",
  "AET Conservancies" = "Amboseli Conservancies",
  "Tsavo West" = "Tsavo West NP",
  "Tsavo East" = "Tsavo East NP",
  "Tsavo Ranches" = "Tsavo Conservancies/Ranches",
  "Tsavo Settled Areas" = "Tsavo Settled Areas"
)

area_colors_zones.noAllZones <- c(
  "Amboseli NP" = "#440154FF",
  "Amboseli Conservancies" = "#5DC863FF",
  "Amboseli Community/Group Ranches" = "#AADC32FF",
  "Tsavo East NP" = "#472D7BFF",
  "Tsavo West NP" = "#3B528BFF",
  "Tsavo Conservancies/Ranches" = "#2C728EFF",
  "Tsavo Settled Areas" = "#21908CFF"
)

# Recode area names in the dataframe
All.RPI.Visual.Areas$Area <- recode(All.RPI.Visual.Areas$Area, !!!area_labels.noAllZones)
All.Means$Area <- recode(All.Means$Area, !!!area_labels.noAllZones)

# Order facets by Area
area_order <- names(area_colors_zones.noAllZones)
All.RPI.Visual.Areas$Area <- factor(All.RPI.Visual.Areas$Area, levels = area_order)
All.Means$Area <- factor(All.Means$Area, levels = area_order)

# The y-axis is limited to 0-1.5 so that the bulk of the distributions can be seen. coord_cartesian() only zooms in: the pixel-years above 1.5 stay in the violins' calculation and are counted in "Numbers reported in the manuscript".
y_limits <- c(0, 1.5)

# Plot (Figure S5)
# The violins are drawn from the retained pixels only (R² ≥ 0.1), because the filter is applied when each zone is cropped. The coloured line is the centred 5-year rolling mean of each zone's annual mean RPI; a centred 5-year mean cannot be calculated for the first two and the last two years, which is why the lines stop short of both ends.
RPI.Distribution.Areas.Plot <- ggplot() +

  # Violin distributions
  geom_violin(
    data = All.RPI.Visual.Areas,
    aes(x = Year, y = RPI_value, group = Year),
    fill = "grey85", color = "grey50",
    alpha = 0.5, width = 0.8, linewidth = 0.15
  ) +

  # Rolling mean lines
  geom_line(
    data = All.Means,
    aes(x = Year, y = RollingMean5, color = Area),
    linewidth = 0.6
  ) +

  # Rolling mean points
  geom_point(
    data = All.Means,
    aes(x = Year, y = RollingMean5, color = Area),
    size = 0.8
  ) +

  # Colour mapping
  scale_color_manual(values = area_colors_zones.noAllZones) +

  # Labels
  labs(
    x = "Hydrological year (start year)",
    y = "Annual RPI"
  ) +

  # Axes
  coord_cartesian(ylim = y_limits) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(min(All.RPI.Visual.Areas$Year),
                 max(All.RPI.Visual.Areas$Year), by = 5)
  ) +

  # Facets (long zone names are wrapped so that they are not cut off)
  facet_wrap(~Area, ncol = 3, scales = "fixed", labeller = label_wrap_gen(width = 18)) +

  # Theme (text sizes are final printed sizes, because the figure is saved at its printed width)
  theme_minimal(base_size = 8) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 7, color = "black"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold")
  )

RPI.Distribution.Areas.Plot
```

```{r}
  plot = RPI.Distribution.Areas.Plot,
  width = 16,
  height = 20,
  units = "cm",
  dpi = 600,

)
```

```{r}
# Calculation of Theil-Sen
```

```{r}
## Theil-Sen across Amboseli NP

# Sorting data by "Year" & "ID"
Amboseli.RPI.Visual.Arranged <- Amboseli.RPI.Visual %>% arrange(ID, Year)

# Split data by pixel ID
Amboseli.Pixel.List <- Amboseli.RPI.Visual.Arranged %>% group_split(ID)

# Apply sens.slope to each pixel group
Amboseli.TheilSen <- map_dfr(Amboseli.Pixel.List, function(df) {
  if (sum(!is.na(df$RPI_value)) >= 3) {
    slope <- tryCatch(
      sens.slope(df$RPI_value)$estimates,
      error = function(e) NA_real_
    )
  } else {
    slope <- NA_real_
  }
  tibble(ID = unique(df$ID), Slope = slope)
})

# Joining slope results back with area info
Amboseli.TheilSen <- Amboseli.TheilSen %>%
  mutate(Area = "Amboseli")

# Getting overall summary per area
Amboseli.SummaryTrend <- Amboseli.TheilSen %>%
  summarise(
    MeanSlope = mean(Slope, na.rm = TRUE),
    MedianSlope = median(Slope, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD = sd(Slope, na.rm = TRUE),
    N = sum(!is.na(Slope))
  )
```

```{r}
# Visualising MeanSlope across study area

All.Pixel.Slopes <- bind_rows(
  Amboseli.TheilSen, TsavoEast.TheilSen, 
  TsavoWest.TheilSen, Tsavo.Ranches.TheilSen,
  Tsavo.SettledAreas.TheilSen, Tsavo.AllZones.TheilSen,
  AET.Conservancies.TheilSen,AET.Buffers.TheilSen, 
  AET.AllZones.TheilSen)


All.Trends.Summary <- All.Pixel.Slopes %>%
  group_by(Area) %>%
  summarise(
    MeanSlope = mean(Slope, na.rm = TRUE),
    MedianSlope = median(Slope, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD = sd(Slope, na.rm = TRUE),
    N = sum(!is.na(Slope)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
## All.Trends.Summary summarises the overall direction and strength of change in RPI for each area over the full time series.

Mean.Slope.Plot <- ggplot(All.Trends.Summary, aes(x = reorder(Area, MeanSlope), y = MeanSlope)) +
  
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = MeanSlope - SD, ymax = MeanSlope + SD),
                width = 0.2, color = "darkgrey") +
  geom_point(aes(color = "Mean Slope"), size = 3, fill = "steelblue", shape = 21) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "darkred") +
  labs(
    title = "Mean RPI Trend (Theil–Sen) by Area with Standard Deviation",
    x = "Area",
    y = "Mean Slope",
    color = "Legend"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

Mean.Slope.Plot
```

```{r}
# Re-defining the custom color palette
areas_colours_names <- c(
  "Amboseli" = "#440154FF",
  "AET.Buffers" = "#AADC32FF",
  "AET.Conservancies" = "#5DC863FF",
  "AET.AllZones" = "#FDE725FF",
  "TsavoEast" = "#472D7BFF",
  "TsavoWest" = "#3B528BFF",
  "Tsavo.Ranches" = "#2C728EFF",
  "Tsavo.SettledAreas" = "#21908CFF",
  "Tsavo.AllZones" = "#27AD81FF"
)

area_labels <- c(
  "Amboseli" = "Amboseli NP",
  "AET.Buffers" = "Amboseli Community/Group Ranches",
  "AET.AllZones" = "Amboseli All Zones",
  "AET.Conservancies" = "Amboseli Conservancies",
  "TsavoWest" = "Tsavo West NP",
  "TsavoEast" = "Tsavo East NP",
  "Tsavo.Ranches" = "Tsavo Conservancies/Ranches",
  "Tsavo.SettledAreas" = "Tsavo Settled Areas",
  "Tsavo.AllZones" = "Tsavo All Zones"
)

# Combining all correctly labeled data frames
All.Pixel.Slopes <- bind_rows(
  Amboseli.TheilSen, TsavoEast.TheilSen,  
  TsavoWest.TheilSen, Tsavo.Ranches.TheilSen,
  Tsavo.SettledAreas.TheilSen, Tsavo.AllZones.TheilSen,
  AET.Conservancies.TheilSen, AET.Buffers.TheilSen,  
  AET.AllZones.TheilSen
)

# Reorder areas by mean slope for a logical plot order
Mean.Slope.Order <- All.Pixel.Slopes %>%
  group_by(Area) %>%
  summarise(MeanSlopeArea = mean(Slope, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(MeanSlopeArea)) %>%
  pull(Area)

# Apply the ordered factor levels to the data frame 
All.Pixel.Slopes$Area <- factor(All.Pixel.Slopes$Area, levels = Mean.Slope.Order)

# Ridgeline plot using assigned colors 
Ridgeline.Plot <- ggplot(All.Pixel.Slopes, aes(x = Slope, y = Area, fill = Area)) +
  geom_density_ridges(
    scale = 3,  
    rel_min_height = 0.01,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", size = 1) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = areas_colours_names,   
    labels = area_labels,           
    name = "Study Area"
  ) +
  
  scale_y_discrete(labels = area_labels) +  
  
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Theil–Sen Slopes per Area",
    x = "Slope",
    y = "Area"
  ) +
  
  theme_ridges(font_size = 14, grid = TRUE) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

Ridgeline.Plot
```

```{r}
# This plot visualizes the overall long-term trend in RPI for eight different areas based on a robust statistical analysis. Each dot represents the mean RPI trend (Theil-Sen slope) for all pixels within a specific area. A positive mean slope (above the red dashed line at zero) indicates an overall increasing RPI trend for that area, while a negative mean slope (below the line) indicates an overall decreasing trend. The error bars extend one standard deviation above and below the mean, representing the variability of trends among the individual pixels within each area. For example, the wide error bars for "TsavoEast" show that while its overall trend is positive, there's a significant amount of variation in RPI trends at the pixel level.
```


```{r}
# This plot, titled "Distribution of RPI Trends (Theil–Sen Slopes) by Area", visually summarises the long-term trend in RPI for each of the study areas. The plot uses a Theil–Sen slope as a robust, non-parametric measure of change, where a positive slope indicates an increasing trend and a negative slope indicates a decreasing trend.

# Each panel represents a different study area, and within each panel, a violin plot shows the full distribution of RPI trends for every single pixel in that area. The width of the violin corresponds to the density of the data, so a wider section means more pixels have that particular slope. A boxplot is overlaid on each violin, with a central line indicating the median slope, and the box representing the interquartile range (the middle 50% of slopes).  The black dot within each violin shows the mean slope for that area.

# The dashed red line at zero serves as a critical reference point. Slopes falling to the right of this line indicate an overall positive (increasing) RPI trend, while slopes to the left indicate a negative (decreasing) trend. This visualization allows for a comprehensive comparison of not just the average trend across areas, but also the spread and variability of those trends, providing a more detailed picture of the RPI changes than a simple bar chart.
```

```{r}
# Creating Raster Maps of Theil-Sen Slopes
```

```{r}
## Amboseli Raster Map of Theil-Sen Slopes

# 1. I shall use the original raster as a template using only 1 layer for structure
Amboseli.Slope.Raster <- terra::rast(Amboseli.RPI.Crop[[1]])
terra::values(Amboseli.Slope.Raster) <- NA  # blank it out

# 2. I shall then link slope values to cell numbers
Amboseli.Cell.Map <- data.frame(ID = 1:nrow(Amboseli.RPI.Values.Full), cell = Amboseli.RPI.Values.Full$cell)

# Merging slopes with cells
Amboseli.Slope.Cells <- dplyr::left_join(Amboseli.TheilSen, Amboseli.Cell.Map, by = "ID")

# 3. Populate slope values into raster cells
Amboseli.Slope.Raster[Amboseli.Slope.Cells$cell] <- Amboseli.Slope.Cells$Slope

# 4. Plot the raster
tm_shape(Amboseli.Slope.Raster) +
  tm_raster(
    col.scale = tm_scale_continuous(values = "brewer.pu_or", midpoint = 0),
    col.legend = tm_legend(title = "Amboseli Theil–Sen Slope", reverse = TRUE)) +
  tm_title("Spatial Distribution of RPI Trends — Amboseli") +
  tm_layout(legend.outside = TRUE)
```

```{r}
  group_by(ProtectionType) %>%
  summarise(
    MeanSlope = mean(Slope, na.rm = TRUE),
    MedianSlope = median(Slope, na.rm = TRUE),

    .groups = "drop"
```

```{r}
# MixedUse = Slight decline, smaller than community lands.

# NationalPark = On average, RPI is increasing inside parks.

# Ranches = Small but positive increase, between mixed use and parks.
```

```{r}
## Yearly summary data

# Combining all pixel values with area info
All.Pixel.Values.RPI.Visual <- bind_rows(
  Amboseli.RPI.Visual, TsavoEast.RPI.Visual, 
  TsavoWest.RPI.Visual, Tsavo.Ranches.RPI.Visual,
  Tsavo.SettledAreas.RPI.Visual,AET.Conservancies.RPI.Visual, 
  AET.Buffers.RPI.Visual)

# Re-calculating the summary to include standard deviation
Annual.RPI.Visual.Trends <- All.Pixel.Values.RPI.Visual %>%
  group_by(Area, Year) %>%
  summarise(
    MeanRPI = mean(RPI_value, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD = sd(RPI_value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Plot with ribbon to show variability
Annual.RPI.Visual.Trends.Faceted.Plot <- ggplot(Annual.RPI.Visual.Trends, aes(x = Year, y = MeanRPI)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = MeanRPI - SD, ymax = MeanRPI + SD, fill = Area), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(aes(color = Area), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(color = Area), size = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Annual Mean RPI Trends with Standard Deviation",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Mean RPI"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ Area, ncol = 3) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

Annual.RPI.Visual.Trends.Faceted.Plot
```

```{r}
# Combined Mean RPI Trends with Theil–Sen Slopes (Figure 4)

area_labels <- c(
  "Amboseli" = "Amboseli NP",
  "AET.Buffers" = "Amboseli Community/Group Ranches",
  "AET.AllZones" = "Amboseli All Zones",
  "AET.Conservancies" = "Amboseli Conservancies",
  "TsavoWest" = "Tsavo West NP",
  "TsavoEast" = "Tsavo East NP",
  "Tsavo.Ranches" = "Tsavo Conservancies/Ranches",
  "Tsavo.SettledAreas" = "Tsavo Settled Areas",
  "Tsavo.AllZones" = "Tsavo All Zones"
)

areas_colours_names <- c(
  "Amboseli" = "#440154FF",
  "AET.Buffers" = "#AADC32FF",
  "AET.Conservancies" = "#5DC863FF",
  "AET.AllZones" = "#FDE725FF",
  "TsavoEast" = "#472D7BFF",
  "TsavoWest" = "#3B528BFF",
  "Tsavo.Ranches" = "#2C728EFF",
  "Tsavo.SettledAreas" = "#21908CFF",
  "Tsavo.AllZones" = "#27AD81FF"
)

# Order of the panels: Amboseli zones first, then Tsavo zones
area_order_panels <- c("Amboseli", "AET.Conservancies", "AET.Buffers",
                       "TsavoEast", "TsavoWest", "Tsavo.Ranches", "Tsavo.SettledAreas")

Combined.Trends <- Annual.RPI.Visual.Trends %>%
  mutate(Area = factor(Area, levels = area_order_panels))

# Theil–Sen line for each zone
# The line drawn in each panel is the Theil–Sen slope of that zone's annual mean RPI series (the 23 points shown in the panel). The intercept is the median of (MeanRPI - Slope * Year), so the line runs through the middle of the series. It is not an ordinary straight-line (lm) fit. This zone-level slope is not the same number as the mean of the pixel-level Theil–Sen slopes reported in the text ("All.Trends.Summary"); both are printed side by side in "Numbers reported in the manuscript".
Zone.TheilSen.Lines <- Annual.RPI.Visual.Trends %>%
  group_by(Area) %>%
  arrange(Year, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  summarise(
    Slope = as.numeric(sens.slope(MeanRPI)$estimates),
    Intercept = median(MeanRPI - Slope * Year),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(Area = factor(Area, levels = area_order_panels))

Zone.TheilSen.Lines

Combined.Trends.Plot <- ggplot(
  Combined.Trends,
  aes(x = Year, y = MeanRPI)
) +

  # Ribbon: spread of pixel values within each year (mean ± 1 standard deviation across pixels). This is spatial variability within the zone, not interannual variability.
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = MeanRPI - SD,
      ymax = MeanRPI + SD,
      fill = Area
    ),
    alpha = 0.15
  ) +

  # Annual Time-Series (Dashed)
  geom_line(
    aes(color = Area),
    linewidth = 0.4,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +

  # Annual Points
  geom_point(
    aes(color = Area),
    size = 0.9
  ) +

  # Theil–Sen Trend Line of the annual zone means (Colour-Coded Solid)
  geom_abline(
    data = Zone.TheilSen.Lines,
    aes(slope = Slope, intercept = Intercept, color = Area),
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +

  # Facets (long zone names are wrapped so that they are not cut off)
  facet_wrap(
    ~ Area,
    ncol = 3,
    scales = "fixed",
    labeller = labeller(Area = function(x) str_wrap(area_labels[as.character(x)], width = 24))
  ) +

  # Colour Scales
  scale_color_manual(values = areas_colours_names) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = areas_colours_names) +

  # Labels
  labs(
    x = "Hydrological year (start year)",
    y = "Mean annual RPI"
  ) +

  # Theme (text sizes are final printed sizes, because the figure is saved at its printed width)
  theme_classic(base_size = 8) +

  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 7, color = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8),
    panel.spacing = unit(0.8, "lines")
  )

Combined.Trends.Plot
```

```{r}
## Clipping Temporal Performance to Kenya Admin Boundary

### Ensure CRS matches
Kenya.Admin.Boundary <- st_transform(Kenya.Admin.Boundary, crs(Temporal.Performance))

### Convert to terra vector
Kenya.Admin.Boundary.Vect <- vect(Kenya.Admin.Boundary)

### Crop and mask
Temporal.Performance.Kenya <- crop(Temporal.Performance, Kenya.Admin.Boundary.Vect)
Temporal.Performance.Kenya <- mask(Temporal.Performance.Kenya, Kenya.Admin.Boundary.Vect, touches = FALSE)
```

```{r}
##  Plotting Temporal Performance clipped to Kenya's Administrative Boundary

ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = Temporal.Performance.Kenya) +
  facet_wrap(~lyr, ncol = 3) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colours = c("lightblue", "limegreen", "yellow", "red"),
    na.value = "grey90"
  ) +
  geom_sf(data = Kenya.Admin.Boundary, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
  labs(

    subtitle = "MAE, RMSE, and R² metrics",
    fill = "Performance"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +

    legend.position = "bottom",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),

  )
```

```{r}
# Each metric (MAE, RMSE, R²) has different units/scales → so they shouldn’t share the same colour scale.

# My current gradient (blue → green → yellow → red) works for error metrics (MAE, RMSE) but is misleading for R² (bounded between 0–1).

# The “R² map” looks blank because most values are between 0 and 1, and this colour scale was probably tuned for much larger values.

#MAE, the mean absolute error between predicted GPP and actual GPP.
# R2, the proportion of GPP variance explained by each method.
# Rppt, the correlation between the resulting values of each index and precipitation, the most important climatic driver of GPP.
# average root mean squared error (RMSE)

# Problem: ggplot2 only allows one scale per aesthetic.To get different colour scales for each facet, I am using "facetted_pos_scales" from libraries ggplot2 + ggforce & "facet_wrap_scales" from library ggh4x.
```

```{r}
# Shared Kenya border layer
Kenya.Border <- geom_sf(data = Kenya.Admin.Boundary, 
                        fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.3)

# MAE plot with a vertical legend

  geom_spatraster(data = Temporal.Performance.Kenya$mae) +
  scale_fill_scico(palette = "roma", name = "MAE", na.value = "grey90") +
  Kenya.Border +
  labs(title = "MAE") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") + # Move legend to the side
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(direction = "vertical"))

# RMSE plot with a vertical legend
Plot.RMSE <- ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = Temporal.Performance.Kenya$rmse) +
  scale_fill_scico(palette = "vik", name = "RMSE", na.value = "grey90") +
  Kenya.Border +
  labs(title = "RMSE") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(direction = "vertical"))

# R² plot with a vertical legend
Plot.Rsqd <- ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = Temporal.Performance.Kenya$rsq) +
  scale_fill_scico(palette = "bam", name = expression(R^2), 
                   limits = c(0, 1), na.value = "grey90") +
  Kenya.Border +
  labs(title = expression(R^2)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(direction = "vertical"))

# Combining with patchwork
```

```{r}
# Tweaking the above map
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(scico)
library(tidyterra)

# Kenya border
Kenya.Border <- geom_sf(
  data = Kenya.Admin.Boundary,
  fill = NA,
  color = "black",
  linewidth = 0.4
)

# MAE
Plot.MAE <- ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = Temporal.Performance.Kenya$mae) +
  scale_fill_scico(
    palette = "lajolla",
    name = "MAE",
    na.value = "grey90"
  ) +
  Kenya.Border +
  coord_sf(expand = FALSE) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_blank()
  )

# RMSE
Plot.RMSE <- ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = Temporal.Performance.Kenya$rmse) +
  scale_fill_scico(
    palette = "batlow",
    name = "RMSE",
    na.value = "grey90"
  ) +
  Kenya.Border +
  coord_sf(expand = FALSE) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_blank()
  )

# R²
Plot.Rsqd <- ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = Temporal.Performance.Kenya$rsq) +
  scale_fill_scico(
    palette = "bam",
    name = expression(R^2),
    limits = c(0, 1),
    na.value = "grey90"
  ) +
  Kenya.Border +
  coord_sf(expand = FALSE) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_blank()
  )

# Combine
Combined.Temporal.Performance.Plot <-
  (Plot.MAE | Plot.RMSE | Plot.Rsqd) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") &
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0)
  )

Combined.Temporal.Performance.Plot
```

```{r}
## R² values for each zone

# The R² layer was cropped to each zone when the zone was first processed ("RSQ.<Zone>"). The R² and RPI layers share one grid, so cropping returns exactly the same cells as the zonal RPI rasters and no resampling is needed. (Bilinear resampling would blend neighbouring R² values and can drop pixels next to gaps.) The checks below confirm that every pair matches in extent, resolution and CRS.

stopifnot(
  compareGeom(RSQ.Amboseli, Amboseli.RPI.Mean),
  compareGeom(RSQ.TsavoEast, TsavoEast.RPI.Mean),
  compareGeom(RSQ.TsavoWest, TsavoWest.RPI.Mean),
  compareGeom(RSQ.Tsavo.Ranches, Tsavo.Ranches.RPI.Mean),
  compareGeom(RSQ.Tsavo.SettledAreas, Tsavo.SettledAreas.RPI.Mean),
  compareGeom(RSQ.Tsavo.AllZones, Tsavo.AllZones.RPI.Mean),
  compareGeom(RSQ.AET.Conservancies, AET.Conservancies.RPI.Mean),
  compareGeom(RSQ.AET.Buffers, AET.Buffers.RPI.Mean),
  compareGeom(RSQ.AET.AllZones, AET.AllZones.RPI.Mean)
)
```

```{r}
# Sensitivity check — not used for the published results. The block below applies an exploratory R² ≥ 0.3 threshold to the unfiltered mean RPI of each zone. It is retained to document the threshold sensitivity assessment only. All results reported in the manuscript use the R² ≥ 0.1 threshold ("RSQ.Threshold.1"), which is applied once, straight after each zone is cropped. Objects created here carry the suffix ".Filtered.3" and are not referenced by any downstream analysis or figure.

# #  Set R² threshold
RSQ.Threshold.3 <- 0.3  # Exploratory sensitivity threshold only; the published analysis uses 0.1 (see below)

# 1. Creating mask for pixels with R² >= threshold
RSQ.Mask.Amboseli <- RSQ.Amboseli >= RSQ.Threshold.3

# 2. Applying the mask to the RPI mean raster
Amboseli.RPI.Mean.Filtered.3 <- mask(Amboseli.RPI.Mean, RSQ.Mask.Amboseli, maskvalues = FALSE)

# 2. Visualising the filtered result
tmap_mode(Map.Mode)
tm_shape(Amboseli.RPI.Mean.Filtered.3) +
  tm_raster(
    col.scale = tm_scale_continuous(values = "viridis"), 
    col.legend = tm_legend(title = "Mean RPI (Filtered by R² ≥ 0.3)", reverse = TRUE)) +
  tm_shape(Amboseli) +
  tm_borders(col = "white", lwd = 2) +
  tm_layout(legend.outside = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# Published quality-control threshold (R² ≥ 0.1)

# The published threshold ("RSQ.Threshold.1") is set and applied once, straight after each zone is cropped (see "Visualising RPI for each Area" above). The mean-RPI maps, the yearly zone means and the Theil–Sen slopes reported in the manuscript therefore all use the same retained pixels. Objects with the suffix ".Filtered.1" hold the mean RPI of those retained pixels; the maps below show them zone by zone.
```

```{r}
# Creating individual map panels
# 1. Set tmap options
tmap_mode("plot")
tmap_options(component.autoscale = FALSE)

# 2. Calculate a global RPI range for consistent coloring
global_rpi_range <- range(c(
  values(Amboseli.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1),
  values(TsavoEast.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1),
  values(TsavoWest.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1),
  values(Tsavo.Ranches.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1),
  values(Tsavo.SettledAreas.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1),
  values(Tsavo.AllZones.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1),
  values(AET.Conservancies.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1),
  values(AET.Buffers.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1),
  values(AET.AllZones.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1)
), na.rm = TRUE)

# 3. Simplify the individual maps
Map.Amboseli.RPI <- tm_shape(Amboseli.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1) +
  tm_raster(col.scale = tm_scale_continuous(values = "viridis", limits = global_rpi_range),
            col.legend = tm_legend(show = FALSE))

Map.TsavoEast.RPI <- tm_shape(TsavoEast.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1) +
  tm_raster(col.scale = tm_scale_continuous(values = "viridis", limits = global_rpi_range),
            col.legend = tm_legend(show = FALSE))

Map.TsavoWest.RPI <- tm_shape(TsavoWest.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1) +
  tm_raster(col.scale = tm_scale_continuous(values = "viridis", limits = global_rpi_range),
            col.legend = tm_legend(show = FALSE))

Map.Tsavo.Ranches.RPI <- tm_shape(Tsavo.Ranches.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1) +
  tm_raster(col.scale = tm_scale_continuous(values = "viridis", limits = global_rpi_range),
            col.legend = tm_legend(show = FALSE))

Map.Tsavo.SettledAreas.RPI <- tm_shape(Tsavo.SettledAreas.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1) +
  tm_raster(col.scale = tm_scale_continuous(values = "viridis", limits = global_rpi_range),
            col.legend = tm_legend(show = FALSE))

Map.Tsavo.AllZones.RPI <- tm_shape(Tsavo.AllZones.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1) +
  tm_raster(col.scale = tm_scale_continuous(values = "viridis", limits = global_rpi_range),
            col.legend = tm_legend(show = FALSE))

Map.AET.Conservancies.RPI <- tm_shape(AET.Conservancies.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1) +
  tm_raster(col.scale = tm_scale_continuous(values = "viridis", limits = global_rpi_range),
            col.legend = tm_legend(show = FALSE))

Map.AET.Buffers.RPI <- tm_shape(AET.Buffers.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1) +
  tm_raster(col.scale = tm_scale_continuous(values = "viridis", limits = global_rpi_range),
            col.legend = tm_legend(show = FALSE))

Map.AET.AllZones.RPI <- tm_shape(AET.AllZones.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1) +
  tm_raster(col.scale = tm_scale_continuous(values = "viridis", limits = global_rpi_range),
            col.legend = tm_legend(title = "Mean RPI", reverse = TRUE))

# 4. Combine and add common elements
Combined.RPI.Maps.After.Filtering <- tmap_arrange(
  Map.Amboseli.RPI + tm_shape(Amboseli) + tm_borders(col = "white", lwd = 1.5) + tm_title("Amboseli"),
  Map.TsavoEast.RPI + tm_shape(TsavoEast) + tm_borders(col = "white", lwd = 1.5) + tm_title("Tsavo East"),
  Map.TsavoWest.RPI + tm_shape(TsavoWest) + tm_borders(col = "white", lwd = 1.5) + tm_title("Tsavo West"),
  Map.Tsavo.Ranches.RPI + tm_shape(Tsavo.Ranches) + tm_borders(col = "white", lwd = 1.5) + tm_title("Tsavo Ranches"),
  Map.Tsavo.SettledAreas.RPI + tm_shape(Tsavo.SettledAreas) + tm_borders(col = "white", lwd = 1.5) + tm_title("Tsavo Settled Areas"),
  Map.Tsavo.AllZones.RPI + tm_shape(Tsavo.AllZones) + tm_borders(col = "white", lwd = 1.5) + tm_title("Tsavo All Zones"),
  Map.AET.Conservancies.RPI + tm_shape(AET.Conservancies) + tm_borders(col = "white", lwd = 1.5) + tm_title("Amboseli Conservancies"),
  Map.AET.Buffers.RPI + tm_shape(AET.Buffers) + tm_borders(col = "white", lwd = 1.5) + tm_title("Amboseli Communitylands"),
  Map.AET.AllZones.RPI + tm_shape(AET.AllZones) + tm_borders(col = "white", lwd = 1.5) + tm_title("Amboseli All Zones"),
  ncol = 3, nrow = 3
)

Combined.RPI.Maps.After.Filtering
```

```{r}
# RPI Summary Statistics before and after filtering (threshold of 0.1)
```

```{r}
# Yearly zone summaries before and after the R² filter

# The filter has already been applied once, straight after each zone was cropped: "<Zone>.RPI.Crop.Unfiltered" holds every pixel in the zone and "<Zone>.RPI.Crop" holds the retained pixels (R² ≥ 0.1). The function below summarises either stack in the same way, so nothing is filtered (or resampled) a second time here.

summarise_rpi_area <- function(rpi_stack, polygon, area_name) {

  vals_full <- terra::extract(rpi_stack, polygon, cells = TRUE)
  vals <- vals_full[, names(rpi_stack)]

  data.frame(
    Area   = area_name,
    Layer  = names(rpi_stack),
    Mean   = apply(vals, 2, mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD     = apply(vals, 2, sd, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q25    = apply(vals, 2, quantile, probs = 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median = apply(vals, 2, median, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q75    = apply(vals, 2, quantile, probs = 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

# RAW summaries (every pixel in each zone, before quality control)
All.Summary.Raw <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  summarise_rpi_area(Amboseli.RPI.Crop.Unfiltered, Amboseli, "Amboseli NP"),
  summarise_rpi_area(AET.Conservancies.RPI.Crop.Unfiltered, AET.Conservancies, "Amboseli Conservancies"),
  summarise_rpi_area(AET.Buffers.RPI.Crop.Unfiltered, AET.Buffers, "Amboseli Community/Group Ranches"),
  summarise_rpi_area(TsavoWest.RPI.Crop.Unfiltered, TsavoWest, "Tsavo West NP"),
  summarise_rpi_area(TsavoEast.RPI.Crop.Unfiltered, TsavoEast, "Tsavo East NP"),
  summarise_rpi_area(Tsavo.Ranches.RPI.Crop.Unfiltered, Tsavo.Ranches, "Tsavo Conservancies/Ranches"),
  summarise_rpi_area(Tsavo.SettledAreas.RPI.Crop.Unfiltered, Tsavo.SettledAreas, "Tsavo Settled Areas")
)

# FILTERED summaries (retained pixels only, R² ≥ 0.1) - these are the values reported in the manuscript
All.Summary.Filtered <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  summarise_rpi_area(Amboseli.RPI.Crop, Amboseli, "Amboseli NP"),
  summarise_rpi_area(AET.Conservancies.RPI.Crop, AET.Conservancies, "Amboseli Conservancies"),
  summarise_rpi_area(AET.Buffers.RPI.Crop, AET.Buffers, "Amboseli Community/Group Ranches"),
  summarise_rpi_area(TsavoWest.RPI.Crop, TsavoWest, "Tsavo West NP"),
  summarise_rpi_area(TsavoEast.RPI.Crop, TsavoEast, "Tsavo East NP"),
  summarise_rpi_area(Tsavo.Ranches.RPI.Crop, Tsavo.Ranches, "Tsavo Conservancies/Ranches"),
  summarise_rpi_area(Tsavo.SettledAreas.RPI.Crop, Tsavo.SettledAreas, "Tsavo Settled Areas")
)

All.Summary.Filtered
```

```{r}
# Define the layers of interest
layers <- paste0("rpi.", 2000:2022)

# Define a helper function
extract_area_values <- function(area_name) {
  All.Summary.Filtered %>%
    filter(Area == area_name,
           Layer %in% layers) %>%
    arrange(Layer)
}

# Apply to each area
Amboseli.NP.Values <- extract_area_values("Amboseli NP")
Amboseli.Conservancies.Values <- extract_area_values("Amboseli Conservancies")
Amboseli.Community.Values <- extract_area_values("Amboseli Community/Group Ranches")
Tsavo.West.Values <- extract_area_values("Tsavo West NP")
Tsavo.East.Values <- extract_area_values("Tsavo East NP")
Tsavo.Conservancies.Values <- extract_area_values("Tsavo Conservancies/Ranches")
Tsavo.Settled.Values <- extract_area_values("Tsavo Settled Areas")
```

```{r}
# MANUSCRIPT AND SI FIGURES AND TABLES

# Every figure and table used in the manuscript and the SI is built and saved by code, with the file name it has in the plots/ folder. Figures are saved at their final printed size (width and height in centimetres, 600 dpi), so text sizes in the code are the sizes on the printed page. Knitting this document rebuilds the plots/ folder.
# Figure 4, Figure S1 and Figure S5 are saved where they are built, earlier in this document. The remaining figures and tables are built below.
```

```{r}
# Shared objects for the figures

# The seven zones in the order used throughout the paper, with their colours
zone_colours <- c(
  "Amboseli NP" = "#440154FF",
  "Amboseli Conservancies" = "#5DC863FF",
  "Amboseli Community/Group Ranches" = "#AADC32FF",
  "Tsavo East NP" = "#472D7BFF",
  "Tsavo West NP" = "#3B528BFF",
  "Tsavo Conservancies/Ranches" = "#2C728EFF",
  "Tsavo Settled Areas" = "#21908CFF"
)

# Study Area Map (focused on areas under study only)

# Defining "make_zone" function
make_zone <- function(sf_layer, zone_name) {
  sf_layer %>%
    select(geometry) %>%  # keep only geometry
    mutate(zone = zone_name)
}

All.Zones.Composite <- bind_rows(
  make_zone(Amboseli, "Amboseli NP"),
  make_zone(AET.Conservancies, "Amboseli Conservancies"),
  make_zone(AET.Buffers, "Amboseli Community/Group Ranches"),
  make_zone(TsavoEast, "Tsavo East NP"),
  make_zone(TsavoWest, "Tsavo West NP"),
  make_zone(Tsavo.Ranches, "Tsavo Conservancies/Ranches"),
  make_zone(Tsavo.SettledAreas, "Tsavo Settled Areas")
) %>%
  mutate(zone = factor(zone, levels = names(zone_colours)))

# Outline of the whole study area (all seven zones merged)
Study.Area.Outline <- st_union(All.Zones.Composite)

# Merge all Rasters into one single object
# The zones do not overlap, so terra::merge simply stitches the zonal rasters together
Combined.RPI.Filtered.1.Raster <- terra::merge(
  Amboseli.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1,
  TsavoEast.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1,
  TsavoWest.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1,
  Tsavo.Ranches.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1,
  Tsavo.SettledAreas.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1,
  AET.Conservancies.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1,
  AET.Buffers.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1
)

# Merge Slope Rasters (Excluding 'All Zones' to avoid redundancy)
Combined.Slope.Raster <- terra::merge(
  Amboseli.Slope.Raster,
  TsavoEast.Slope.Raster,
  TsavoWest.Slope.Raster,
  Tsavo.Ranches.Slope.Raster,
  Tsavo.SettledAreas.Slope.Raster,
  AET.Conservancies.Slope.Raster,
  AET.Buffers.Slope.Raster
)

# Map theme and map furniture, sized for the printed page
theme_map <- theme_void(base_size = 8) +
  theme(
    legend.title = element_text(size = 8, color = "black"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 7, color = "black"),
    legend.key.size = unit(0.35, "cm"),
    plot.margin = margin(2, 2, 2, 2)
  )

map_scale_bar <- function(location = "bl") {
  annotation_scale(
    location = location,
    width_hint = 0.25,
    height = unit(0.12, "cm"),
    text_cex = 0.6,
    line_width = 0.3
  )
}

map_north_arrow <- function(location = "tl") {
  annotation_north_arrow(
    location = location,
    height = unit(0.7, "cm"),
    width = unit(0.45, "cm"),
    style = north_arrow_orienteering(text_size = 5, line_width = 0.4)
  )
}

# Panel labels in the form (A), (B), (C)
panel_tags <- plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A", tag_prefix = "(", tag_suffix = ")")
panel_tag_theme <- theme(plot.tag = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"))

# Labels for a colour scale whose ends are capped: values beyond the limits are drawn in the end colour, and the end labels say so
capped_labels <- function(breaks, accuracy = 1, lower = FALSE, upper = TRUE) {
  lab <- scales::number(breaks, accuracy = accuracy, big.mark = ",")
  if (upper) lab[length(lab)] <- paste0("≥ ", lab[length(lab)])
  if (lower) lab[1] <- paste0("≤ ", lab[1])
  lab
}

# Wrap long zone names over several lines; a name may also break after a "/"
wrap_zone_label <- function(x, width = 20) {
  x <- str_wrap(gsub("/", "/ ", x, fixed = TRUE), width = width)
  gsub("/ ", "/", x, fixed = TRUE)
}

# The governance-zone map used as panel (B) of Figures 2 and 3. It has no legend of its own: the zones are named in panel (C), which uses the same colours.
Zones.Map.Panel <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = All.Zones.Composite, aes(fill = zone), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.12) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = zone_colours) +
  theme_map +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

Zones.Map.Panel
```

```{r}
  as.data.frame(c(TsavoEast.RPI.Mean, RSQ.TsavoEast), na.rm = TRUE) %>% setNames(c("RPI", "RSQ")) %>% mutate(Area = "Tsavo East NP"),

Zone.Pixel.Slopes <- bind_rows(
```

```{r}
# How many pixels the R² filter keeps in each zone (Table S3)

# Number of pixels with a value in a raster
count_pixels <- function(r) sum(!is.na(values(r)))

Pixel.Retention.Table <- tibble(
  Area = names(zone_colours),
  Pixels_Before = c(
    count_pixels(Amboseli.RPI.Mean),
    count_pixels(AET.Conservancies.RPI.Mean),
    count_pixels(AET.Buffers.RPI.Mean),
    count_pixels(TsavoEast.RPI.Mean),
    count_pixels(TsavoWest.RPI.Mean),
    count_pixels(Tsavo.Ranches.RPI.Mean),
    count_pixels(Tsavo.SettledAreas.RPI.Mean)
  ),
  Pixels_After = c(
    count_pixels(Amboseli.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1),
    count_pixels(AET.Conservancies.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1),
    count_pixels(AET.Buffers.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1),
    count_pixels(TsavoEast.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1),
    count_pixels(TsavoWest.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1),
    count_pixels(Tsavo.Ranches.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1),
    count_pixels(Tsavo.SettledAreas.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1)
  )
)

# Totals for the six focal governance zones (Tsavo Settled Areas are shown for context only) and for all seven zones
Pixel.Retention.Table <- bind_rows(
  Pixel.Retention.Table,
  Pixel.Retention.Table %>%
    filter(Area != "Tsavo Settled Areas") %>%
    summarise(Area = "Six focal zones combined", Pixels_Before = sum(Pixels_Before), Pixels_After = sum(Pixels_After)),
  Pixel.Retention.Table %>%
    summarise(Area = "All seven zones combined", Pixels_Before = sum(Pixels_Before), Pixels_After = sum(Pixels_After))
) %>%
  mutate(
    Pixels_Removed = Pixels_Before - Pixels_After,
    Percent_Retained = round(100 * Pixels_After / Pixels_Before, 1)
  )

Pixel.Retention.Table

# Check: the same counts are obtained from the paired RPI and R² values
stopifnot(
  all(Pixel.Retention.Table$Pixels_Before[1:7] == as.integer(table(factor(RSQ.Pixel.Values$Area, levels = names(zone_colours))))),
  all(Pixel.Retention.Table$Pixels_After[1:7] == as.integer(table(factor(RPI.Pixel.Means$Area, levels = names(zone_colours)))))
)

# Save as Word document
Pixel.Retention.Flex <- Pixel.Retention.Table %>%
  rename(
    `Governance zone` = Area,
    `Pixels before filtering` = Pixels_Before,
    `Pixels retained (R² ≥ 0.1)` = Pixels_After,
    `Pixels removed` = Pixels_Removed,
    `% retained` = Percent_Retained
  ) %>%
  flextable() %>%
  set_caption("Number of RPI pixels in each governance zone before and after the R² ≥ 0.1 quality-control filter") %>%
  theme_booktabs() %>%
  autofit()

save_as_docx(Pixel.Retention.Flex, path = here::here("plots", "Table_S3_pixels_retained_after_R2_filter.docx"))
```

```{r}
# Distribution of pixel-level mean RPI in each zone (Figure 2C)

# Every value plotted is the mean RPI of one retained pixel ("RPI.Pixel.Means"). The vertical line in each ridge is the median.

# Order the zones from lowest (bottom) to highest (top) median mean RPI
Median.RPI.Order <- RPI.Pixel.Means %>%
  group_by(Area) %>%
  summarise(MedianRPI_Area = median(RPI)) %>%
  arrange(MedianRPI_Area) %>%
  pull(Area)

RPI.Pixel.Means$Area <- factor(RPI.Pixel.Means$Area, levels = Median.RPI.Order)

RPI.Ridgeline.Plot <- ggplot(RPI.Pixel.Means, aes(x = RPI, y = Area, fill = Area)) +

  ) +

    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 8),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
```

```{r}
# FIGURE S2: Model performance (MAE, RMSE, R²) across Kenya

# One figure with three panels and one caption. Each metric has its own continuous, colour-blind-friendly (viridis) scale. MAE and RMSE have a few very large values, so their scales are capped at the 99th percentile; R² is capped at 0 because a few pixels are strongly negative. Capped values are drawn in the end colour and the end label says so.

performance_map <- function(layer, legend_title, limits, breaks, labels) {
  ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = Kenya.Admin.Boundary, fill = "grey90", colour = NA) +
    geom_spatraster(data = layer, maxcell = 2e6) +
    geom_sf(data = Kenya.Admin.Boundary, fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.2) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(
      name = legend_title,
      limits = limits,
      oob = scales::squish,
      breaks = breaks,
      labels = labels,
      na.value = "transparent"
    ) +
    guides(fill = guide_colourbar(
      title.position = "top",
      barwidth = unit(3.6, "cm"),
      barheight = unit(0.25, "cm")
    )) +
    theme_map +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}

# Upper limits for the MAE and RMSE colour scales (99th percentile, rounded up to the nearest 100)
MAE.Upper <- ceiling(as.numeric(global(Temporal.Performance.Kenya[["mae"]], quantile, probs = 0.99, na.rm = TRUE)) / 100) * 100
RMSE.Upper <- ceiling(as.numeric(global(Temporal.Performance.Kenya[["rmse"]], quantile, probs = 0.99, na.rm = TRUE)) / 100) * 100

MAE.Breaks <- seq(0, MAE.Upper, length.out = 5)
RMSE.Breaks <- seq(0, RMSE.Upper, length.out = 5)
RSQ.Breaks <- seq(0, 1, 0.25)

Figure.S2 <- (
  performance_map(
    Temporal.Performance.Kenya[["mae"]],
    expression("MAE (g C m"^-2 * " yr"^-1 * ")"),
    limits = c(0, MAE.Upper), breaks = MAE.Breaks, labels = capped_labels(MAE.Breaks)
  ) |
    performance_map(
      Temporal.Performance.Kenya[["rmse"]],
      expression("RMSE (g C m"^-2 * " yr"^-1 * ")"),
      limits = c(0, RMSE.Upper), breaks = RMSE.Breaks, labels = capped_labels(RMSE.Breaks)
    ) |
    performance_map(
      Temporal.Performance.Kenya[["rsq"]],
      expression(R^2),
      limits = c(0, 1), breaks = RSQ.Breaks, labels = capped_labels(RSQ.Breaks, accuracy = 0.01, lower = TRUE, upper = FALSE)
    )
) +
  panel_tags &
  panel_tag_theme

Figure.S2

ggsave(
  here::here("plots", "Figure_S2_model_performance_Kenya.png"),
  plot = Figure.S2,
  width = 16,
  height = 8.5,
  units = "cm",
  dpi = 600,
  bg = "white"
)
```

```{r}
# FIGURE S3: Why pixels with R² < 0.1 are excluded

# Mean RPI and R² of every RPI v2 pixel in Kenya (before any filtering)
RPI.Mean.EA <- app(RPI, mean, na.rm = TRUE)

RPI.Mean.Kenya <- mask(crop(RPI.Mean.EA, Kenya.Admin.Boundary), Kenya.Admin.Boundary, touches = FALSE)

RSQ.Kenya <- mask(crop(RSQ.Layer, Kenya.Admin.Boundary), Kenya.Admin.Boundary, touches = FALSE)

# Convert to Data Frame
Kenya.Values.RPI.Rsquare <- as.data.frame(c(RPI.Mean.Kenya, RSQ.Kenya), na.rm = TRUE)
colnames(Kenya.Values.RPI.Rsquare) <- c("RPI", "RSQ")

# (A) Where the excluded pixels are. Pixels are classed as retained (R² ≥ 0.1) or excluded (R² < 0.1), the same rule as the filter. Kenya is drawn in dark grey underneath, so areas outside the RPI v2 product show as dark grey.
Kenya.QC.Class <- classify(
  RSQ.Kenya,
  rcl = matrix(c(-Inf, RSQ.Threshold.1, 1,
                 RSQ.Threshold.1, Inf, 0), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE),
  right = FALSE
)
levels(Kenya.QC.Class) <- data.frame(id = c(0, 1), class = c("Retained", "Excluded"))

Kenya.Plot.Rsq.Low <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = Kenya.Admin.Boundary, fill = "grey45", colour = NA) +
  geom_spatraster(data = Kenya.QC.Class, maxcell = Inf) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = NULL,
    values = c("Retained" = "grey88", "Excluded" = "#D55E00"),
    labels = c("Retained" = expression(R^2 >= 0.1 ~ "(retained)"), "Excluded" = expression(R^2 < 0.1 ~ "(excluded)")),
    na.value = "transparent",
    na.translate = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_sf(data = Kenya.Admin.Boundary, fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.2) +
  # Outline of the Amboseli-Tsavo study area
  geom_sf(data = Study.Area.Outline, fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.35) +
  theme_map +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")

# (B) Mean RPI against R². A few extreme pixels stretch the R² axis to about -39, which hides the threshold, so the axis starts at -2. The pixels left off the axis are counted in "Numbers reported in the manuscript".
Kenya.RSQ.Axis.Minimum <- -2

Kenya.RPI.Rsquare.Plot <- ggplot(
  Kenya.Values.RPI.Rsquare %>% filter(RSQ >= Kenya.RSQ.Axis.Minimum),
  aes(x = RSQ, y = RPI)
) +
  geom_hex(bins = 60) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "D",
    trans = "log10",
    name = "Pixels per hexagon",
    labels = scales::label_comma()
  ) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = RSQ.Threshold.1, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", linewidth = 0.4) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(Kenya.RSQ.Axis.Minimum, 1)) +
  labs(
    x = expression(R^2),
    y = "Mean RPI"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 8) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 7, color = "black"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
    legend.key.height = unit(0.5, "cm"),
    legend.key.width = unit(0.25, "cm")
  )

Figure.S3 <- (Kenya.Plot.Rsq.Low | Kenya.RPI.Rsquare.Plot) +
  plot_layout(widths = c(1, 1.15)) +
  panel_tags &
  panel_tag_theme

Figure.S3

ggsave(

  plot = Figure.S3,

  height = 9.5,
```

```{r}
# TABLE S1: Pixels with mean RPI above 1 in each zone

# Compute proportion with RPI > 1 per area, from the mean RPI of the retained pixels
RPI.Above1.Table <- RPI.Pixel.Means %>%
  mutate(Area = as.character(Area)) %>%
  group_by(Area) %>%
  summarise(
    Total_Pixels = n(),
    Pixels_Above_1 = sum(RPI > 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    Proportion = round(Pixels_Above_1 / Total_Pixels, 4),
    Percentage = round(Proportion * 100, 2)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Percentage))
```

```{r}
## Pixel size and zone areas (Methods "Temporal and trend analysis")

# The RPI grid is in geographic coordinates (degrees), so a pixel is not exactly 500 m x 500 m (0.25 km²). cellSize() gives the true area of every pixel, and areas are therefore summed pixel by pixel rather than calculated as "pixel count x 0.25".
Pixel.Area.km2 <- cellSize(RPI[[1]], unit = "km")

# Total area (km²) of the pixels that have a value in a raster
pixel_area_sum <- function(r) {
  a <- crop(Pixel.Area.km2, r)
  sum(values(a)[!is.na(values(r))])
}

Zone.Area.Table <- tibble(
  Area = names(zone_colours),
  Polygon_km2 = c(
    area_km2(Amboseli), area_km2(AET.Conservancies), area_km2(AET.Buffers),
    area_km2(TsavoEast), area_km2(TsavoWest), area_km2(Tsavo.Ranches), area_km2(Tsavo.SettledAreas)
  ),
  Pixels_Before = Pixel.Retention.Table$Pixels_Before[1:7],
  Pixel_Area_Before_km2 = c(
    pixel_area_sum(Amboseli.RPI.Mean), pixel_area_sum(AET.Conservancies.RPI.Mean), pixel_area_sum(AET.Buffers.RPI.Mean),
    pixel_area_sum(TsavoEast.RPI.Mean), pixel_area_sum(TsavoWest.RPI.Mean), pixel_area_sum(Tsavo.Ranches.RPI.Mean),
    pixel_area_sum(Tsavo.SettledAreas.RPI.Mean)
  ),
  Pixels_After = Pixel.Retention.Table$Pixels_After[1:7],
  Pixel_Area_After_km2 = c(
    pixel_area_sum(Amboseli.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1), pixel_area_sum(AET.Conservancies.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1),
    pixel_area_sum(AET.Buffers.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1), pixel_area_sum(TsavoEast.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1),
    pixel_area_sum(TsavoWest.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1), pixel_area_sum(Tsavo.Ranches.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1),
    pixel_area_sum(Tsavo.SettledAreas.RPI.Mean.Filtered.1)
  )
) %>%
  mutate(Mean_Pixel_km2 = Pixel_Area_Before_km2 / Pixels_Before)

# Polygon_km2 = area of the zone boundary; Pixel_Area_Before_km2 = area of the RPI pixels inside it (smaller than the polygon wherever the RPI v2 product has no data); Pixel_Area_After_km2 = area of the pixels retained after the R² filter
knitr::kable(Zone.Area.Table, digits = c(0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 4))

# Areas recorded in the WDPA files for the three national parks (reported area and GIS area, km²), for comparison with Polygon_km2
bind_rows(
  st_drop_geometry(Amboseli)[, c("NAME", "REP_AREA", "GIS_AREA")],
  st_drop_geometry(TsavoEast)[, c("NAME", "REP_AREA", "GIS_AREA")],
  st_drop_geometry(TsavoWest)[, c("NAME", "REP_AREA", "GIS_AREA")]
)

# Overlaps between the zone polygons as supplied (km²), before every pixel was assigned to one zone
knitr::kable(Zone.Overlaps.Before)
```

```{r}
## Model performance across Kenya (Methods "Model validation and quality control"; Figures S2 and S3)

# Summary of the three performance layers over every RPI v2 pixel inside Kenya's national boundary. (The RPI v2 product only has values for rangeland pixels, so these are the rangeland pixels of Kenya.)
Kenya.Performance.Summary <- as.data.frame(Temporal.Performance.Kenya, na.rm = TRUE) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Metric", values_to = "Value") %>%
  group_by(Metric) %>%
  summarise(
    Pixels = n(),
    Median = median(Value),
    Mean = mean(Value),
    SD = sd(Value),
    Min = min(Value),
    Max = max(Value)
  )

knitr::kable(Kenya.Performance.Summary, digits = 2)

# Share of Kenya's RPI v2 pixels below the R² threshold, and the pixels left off the R² axis of Figure S3B
cat("Kenya: pixels with R² < 0.1:", sum(Kenya.Values.RPI.Rsquare$RSQ < RSQ.Threshold.1), "of", nrow(Kenya.Values.RPI.Rsquare),
    "(", round(100 * mean(Kenya.Values.RPI.Rsquare$RSQ < RSQ.Threshold.1), 2), "%)\n")
cat("Kenya: pixels with R² <", Kenya.RSQ.Axis.Minimum, "(not shown in Figure S3B):", sum(Kenya.Values.RPI.Rsquare$RSQ < Kenya.RSQ.Axis.Minimum),
    "(", round(100 * mean(Kenya.Values.RPI.Rsquare$RSQ < Kenya.RSQ.Axis.Minimum), 3), "%)\n")
cat("Kenya: R² of pixels with mean RPI > 1: median", round(median(Kenya.Values.RPI.Rsquare$RSQ[Kenya.Values.RPI.Rsquare$RPI > 1]), 2), "\n")
```

```{r}
## Pixels retained by the R² filter (Methods; Table S3; Figure S6; response to Reviewer 2)

knitr::kable(Pixel.Retention.Table)

# R² range in each zone before filtering, and the pixels left off the axis of Figure S6
RSQ.Pixel.Values %>%
  mutate(Area = factor(Area, levels = names(zone_colours))) %>%
  group_by(Area) %>%
  summarise(
    Pixels = n(),
    Min_RSQ = min(RSQ),
    Median_RSQ = median(RSQ),
    Max_RSQ = max(RSQ),
    Pixels_Below_Axis = sum(RSQ < Zone.RSQ.Axis.Minimum)
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

# Effect of the filter on the extreme values of pixel-level mean RPI in each zone
RSQ.Pixel.Values %>%
  mutate(Area = factor(Area, levels = names(zone_colours))) %>%
  group_by(Area) %>%
  summarise(
    Min_Before = min(RPI),
    Min_After = min(RPI[RSQ >= RSQ.Threshold.1]),
    Max_Before = max(RPI),
    Max_After = max(RPI[RSQ >= RSQ.Threshold.1])
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

# Does every retained pixel have a complete 23-year series? (Years = number of years with a value; Pixels = number of pixels)
All.Pixel.Values.RPI.Visual %>%
  count(Area, ID, name = "Years") %>%
  count(Area, Years, name = "Pixels") %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r}
## Mean RPI (Results "Spatial patterns and temporal dynamics of mean relative productivity"; Figure 2; Table S1)

# Summary statistics of a set of values
summarise_values <- function(x) {
  tibble(
    N = length(x),
    Min = min(x),
    Q25 = unname(quantile(x, 0.25)),
    Median = median(x),
    Mean = mean(x),
    Q75 = unname(quantile(x, 0.75)),
    Max = max(x)
  )
}

# Pixel-level mean RPI across the combined study area
bind_rows(
  summarise_values(RPI.Pixel.Means$RPI[RPI.Pixel.Means$Area != "Tsavo Settled Areas"]) %>% mutate(Zones = "Six focal zones combined", .before = 1),
  summarise_values(RPI.Pixel.Means$RPI) %>% mutate(Zones = "All seven zones combined", .before = 1)
) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

# Pixel-level mean RPI in each zone
RPI.Pixel.Means %>%
  mutate(Area = factor(as.character(Area), levels = names(zone_colours))) %>%
  group_by(Area) %>%
  summarise(summarise_values(RPI)) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

# Annual mean RPI of each zone: the statistics quoted zone by zone in the Results
# Median, range (with the years in which the lowest and highest annual means occurred) and interquartile range of the 23 annual zone means; the number of years with an annual mean below 0.50; the range of the annual standard deviations; and the change between the first and last year
Annual.Zone.Summary <- All.Summary.Filtered %>%
  mutate(
    Year = as.integer(sub("rpi\\.", "", Layer)),
    Area = factor(Area, levels = names(zone_colours))
  ) %>%
  group_by(Area) %>%
  summarise(
    Median_Annual_Mean = median(Mean),
    Min_Annual_Mean = min(Mean),
    Year_Of_Min = Year[which.min(Mean)],
    Max_Annual_Mean = max(Mean),
    Year_Of_Max = Year[which.max(Mean)],
    Q25_Annual_Mean = unname(quantile(Mean, 0.25)),
    Q75_Annual_Mean = unname(quantile(Mean, 0.75)),
    Years_Below_0.50 = sum(Mean < 0.50),
    Min_Annual_SD = min(SD),
    Max_Annual_SD = max(SD),
    Mean_2000 = Mean[Year == 2000],
    Mean_2022 = Mean[Year == 2022],
    Percent_Change_2000_To_2022 = 100 * (Mean_2022 - Mean_2000) / Mean_2000
  )

knitr::kable(Annual.Zone.Summary, digits = 2)

# Table S1: pixels with mean RPI above 1
knitr::kable(RPI.Above1.Table)

# Figure 2: pixels drawn in the top colour of panel A (mean RPI > 1) and pixels beyond the x-axis of panel C (mean RPI > 1.5)
cat("Pixels with mean RPI > 1:", sum(RPI.Pixel.Means$RPI > 1), "of", nrow(RPI.Pixel.Means),
    "(", round(100 * mean(RPI.Pixel.Means$RPI > 1), 2), "%)\n")
cat("Pixels with mean RPI > 1.5 (beyond the x-axis of Figure 2C):", sum(RPI.Pixel.Means$RPI > 1.5), "\n")

# Figure S5: pixel-years above the y-axis limit of 1.5
cat("Pixel-years with annual RPI > 1.5 (above the y-axis of Figure S5):", sum(All.RPI.Visual.Areas$RPI_value > 1.5), "of", nrow(All.RPI.Visual.Areas),
    "(", round(100 * mean(All.RPI.Visual.Areas$RPI_value > 1.5), 2), "%)\n")
```

```{r}
## Theil-Sen trends (Results "Long-term trends in relative vegetation productivity"; Figures 3 and 4)

# Pixel-level slopes across the combined study area
bind_rows(
  summarise_values(Zone.Pixel.Slopes$Slope[Zone.Pixel.Slopes$Area != "Tsavo Settled Areas"]) %>% mutate(Zones = "Six focal zones combined", .before = 1),
  summarise_values(Zone.Pixel.Slopes$Slope) %>% mutate(Zones = "All seven zones combined", .before = 1)
) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 4)

# Pixel-level slopes in each zone: number of pixels, mean, median and standard deviation of the slopes, and how many standard deviations the mean lies from zero. The last column is the Theil-Sen slope of the zone's annual mean RPI series, which is the line drawn in Figure 4.
Zone.Slope.Summary <- Zone.Pixel.Slopes %>%
  mutate(Area = factor(as.character(Area), levels = names(zone_colours))) %>%
  group_by(Area) %>%
  summarise(
    N_Pixels = n(),
    MeanSlope = mean(Slope),
    MedianSlope = median(Slope),
    SD = sd(Slope),
    Mean_In_SD_From_Zero = MeanSlope / SD
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    Zone.TheilSen.Lines %>%
      transmute(
        Area = factor(recode(as.character(Area), !!!area_labels), levels = names(zone_colours)),
        Slope_Of_Annual_Zone_Means = Slope
      ),
    by = "Area"
  )

knitr::kable(Zone.Slope.Summary, digits = c(0, 0, 5, 5, 5, 2, 5))

# Figure 3: pixels drawn in the end colours of panel A (slope beyond the limits of the colour scale) and pixels beyond the x-axis of panel C (slope beyond -0.03 or +0.03)
cat("Pixels with |slope| >", max(Slope.Limits), "(end colours of Figure 3A):", sum(abs(Zone.Pixel.Slopes$Slope) > max(Slope.Limits)), "of", nrow(Zone.Pixel.Slopes),
    "(", round(100 * mean(abs(Zone.Pixel.Slopes$Slope) > max(Slope.Limits)), 2), "%)\n")
cat("Pixels with |slope| > 0.03 (beyond the x-axis of Figure 3C):", sum(abs(Zone.Pixel.Slopes$Slope) > 0.03),
    "(", round(100 * mean(abs(Zone.Pixel.Slopes$Slope) > 0.03), 2), "%)\n")
```
